Motivation

Understand the laminar nonpremixed CH4-air flame behavior under 
1g and 0g conditions when an axial electric field is applied to the 
flame using three different burner configurations 
(extruded, flush and jet) by using numerical simulations.

Results 
Flush burner geometry
At saturation (-4945.83V)

•
The extruded burner geometry shows an I-V curve similar to the one obtained in the experiments in a 1g 
environment. Changes in the boundary condition have to still be performed.
•
The saturation point in the I-V curve obtained using the flush burner geometry simulation is aligning with 
the one obtained experimentally. The peak of positive charges (H3O+) that reach the upper electrode (anode) 
is displaced from the center, aligning with the experimental observations. However, simulations at sub-
saturation regimes show that higher e-fields are needed in the simulation in order to get the same ion 
currents (z-direction) than the ones obtained experimentally. This might be caused by the interaction 
between burner (positive electrode) and reaction zone. More investigation has to be performed in order to 
clarify this phenomena.
Next steps:
•
Define why sub-saturation flush burner geometry simulations show that higher electric fields are needed to 
achieve the ion currents obtained experimentally.
•
Proceed by simulating jet geometry burner flames at 1g.
•
Proceed by simulating the three burner geometries at 0g.
ASGSR Annual meeting. Oct. 31- Nov 3, 2018. clopezca@uci.edu
